protocol: Commercial DC-8-61, in flight after reported inability to pressurize. 100% oxygen ordered per FAA account. The altitude is the aircraft flight level. Actual cabin pressure and oxygen delivery were not measured in the published reports.
outcome_window: NTSB crew statements place radio nonresponse near FL290 while climbing. The FAA narrative places rapid incapacitation after about four minutes at FL330. These are different observations of impairment. First clinical symptom time and cabin pressure history are unknown. Clinical follow-up duration and final disposition are not reported in the FAA case.
locator: FAA case, Sequence of Events, Medical Findings and Discussion; NTSB NYC94LA062 final report, pp. 1, 3, 5 and 6, Analysis and Factual Information
note: One clinically described pilot from a selected commercial cargo incident. The FAA medical authors describe mixed DCS and arterial gas embolism features. The NTSB investigation attributes incapacitation to decompression sickness. The clinical case is indexed once as mixed decompression illness. No inception cohort or independent exposure denominator is available.
